newsitem.title: USA: Rap star Shakur, shot four times in ambush, dies.
newsitem.headline: Rap star Shakur, shot four times in ambush, dies.

text.p: Rap music star Tupac Shakur, whose tumultuous life often resembled a gangster movie, died on Friday six days after his car was sprayed with bullets in a mysterious ambush, a Las Vegas hospital said.

Shakur, who was shot four times, died at the University Medical Centre in Las Vegas at 4:03 p.m. Pacific time (2303 GMT) on Friday, the hospital said in a short statement. It said the cause of death was "respiratory failure and cardiopulmonary arrest."
Shakur, 25, one of the most notorious performers of hardcore "Gangsta" rap, had been in critical condition since Saturday night's shooting near the famed Las Vegas strip.

He had his right lung removed in one of two operations last Sunday. The hospital had released little information about his condition but hospital sources said he had been on life support since the surgery.

Shakur is best known for raw lyrics laced with violence, sex and profanity describing life in the black ghetto. His latest album, "All Eyez on Me," released this year, celebrated his own outlaw image and sold several million copies.

Beloved by his fans -- and detested by politicians -- for songs that celebrated violence and misogyny, Shakur was no stranger to trouble, having spent much of the last two-and-a-half years in court, prison or hospitals.

The violent last chapter in his life came last Saturday night when the rap star and friends were driving to a nightclub in a convoy after watching the Mike Tyson-Bruce Seldon world heavyweight title fight in Las Vegas.

When the black BMW Shakur was riding in stopped at a red traffic light, a white Cadillac pulled up alongside and a gunman inside fired at least nine bullets, apparently aimed at the passenger seat where Shakur was sitting. The singer and actor was hit four times.

Marion "Suge" Knight, 31, co-founder of Los Angeles-based Death Row Records who produced Shakur's records, was driving the BMW. He was grazed in the head by a bullet fragment but suffered only minor injuries.

No arrests were made. Police said they had only the sketchiest description of the Cadillac and its occupants and did not know the motive for the shooting. A surveillance tape filmed at the boxing match showed Shakur got into an argument with an unknown man there but police did not believe the incident was linked to the shooting.

Las Vegas police spokesman Phil Roland said on Friday police were still at "step one" in the investigation. Police said Knight and other Shakur associates in the convoy gave them little useful information.
Police said two to four men were in the white Cadillac, thought to have California or Nevada plates. They offered a $1,000 reward for information.
Roland said earlier on Friday that police were hoping that Shakur would recover so they could talk to him. "He's probably the most valuable witness," he said.
Tupac Amaru Shakur had a short and turbulent life.

Born in New York in 1971, he spent much of his childhood in poverty. His mother was Afeni Shakur, one of a group of Black Panthers charged with plotting some bombings in the late 1960s. She gave birth to him one month after her acquittal and release from prison. His father was never identified.
In November 1994 Shakur was shot five times while being robbed of $40,000 in jewels in the lobby of a Manhattan recording studio.

In February 1995 he was sentenced to prison for involvement in a sexual attack on a 21-year-old woman in a New York hotel room. He spent eight months behind bars until he was released pending his appeal.
He had forebodings of a violent ending. "All good niggers, all the niggers who change the world, die in violence. They don't die in regular ways," he told Details magazine earlier this year.
